Traced through the invariant to make sure I followed the V2 runner flow:

- The `toolInput.has(id)` replacement for `inputEnded` is faithful because `fragments.end` runs `chunks.delete(id)` after the publish callback, so `has` flips to false at the same point `inputEnded` used to flip to true. The duplicate-end / delta-after-end guards keep the same semantics.
- The `retryEvidence` removal in `tool-result` / `tool-error` is safe since both cases guard on `tool.called`, which is only set in the `tool-call` case — and that case already sets `retryEvidence = true` first, so the later assignments were redundant.

Nice simplification — fewer parallel sources of truth for the same state.

### Update: current OpenCode behavior (v1.17.18)

I re-checked this on Windows with OpenCode `1.17.18`.

The important correction is that current OpenCode already sends:

```http
X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-06-01
```

for both GitHub Copilot model discovery and LLM requests. So the `400k` value in `~/.cache/opencode/models.json` is not evidence that current OpenCode is omitting the header.

With normal live Copilot discovery, OpenCode currently reports:

```text
github-copilot/gpt-5.5
context: 1050000
input:   922000
output:  128000
```

I removed my local manual `gpt-5.5` limit override and custom header plugin, then verified the same `1.05M / 922k / 128k` result with:

```text
opencode models github-copilot --verbose --pure
```

The remaining discrepancy is specifically the fallback path:

```text
Live Copilot /models with OAuth + API version header: 1.05M / 922k / 128k
models.dev static cache:                            400k / 272k / 128k
```

Therefore, when live Copilot discovery succeeds, current OpenCode behaves correctly. If that live request fails due to network/proxy/timeout, it can fall back to the smaller static metadata and become conservatively limited to 400k for that startup.

This issue is still useful as documentation of the two-source mismatch, but the likely fix is no longer “add the API version header.” The relevant question is whether the fallback metadata should be updated, or whether OpenCode should retain the last successful account-specific Copilot model metadata.

I don't think coalescing by `sessionID + action` is correct here.

  The bug in #36055 is about duplicate pending requests for the same effective
  permission scope, not about all requests of the same permission type being
  interchangeable.

  In `v2/packages/core/src/permission.ts`, permission evaluation and saved rules are
  resource-scoped:
  - permission decisions are evaluated per `action + resource`
  - remembered rules are saved with `action + resources`

  Because of that, two requests with the same `action` but different resources are
  not necessarily equivalent. For example, two `fs_write` requests targeting
  different files should not automatically piggyback on the same approval.

  The issue case should be fixed by coalescing only semantically equivalent pending
  requests, e.g. same session, same action, and same effective resource scope
  (`resources` / `patterns`, and likely `save` / `always` as well after
  normalization).

  As written, this PR seems to widen one approval to unrelated resources, which
  changes permission semantics instead of just deduplicating duplicate prompts.

This was implemented and then lost track of, rather than never built. Tracing it, in case it saves someone the dig:

- **#8359** (@tomzhu1024) added `packages/opencode/src/provider/model-detection.ts` plus the wiring in `provider.ts`. It was merged on 2026-01-30, but into the staging branch `models-endpoint`, not `dev`.
- **#13234** (@rekram1-node) was opened 2026-02-12 to bring `models-endpoint` into `dev`.
- #13234 was closed unmerged on 2026-05-15 by the automated stale-PR cleanup.

The branch still exists and still has the code. It's now ~5,700 commits behind `dev`.

The interesting part is that half of that work *is* live on `dev` today. `provider.ts` builds a generic `discoveryLoaders` map, populated for any provider that implements `discoverModels`:

```ts
if (result.discoverModels) discoveryLoaders[providerID] = result.discoverModels
```

...but there is exactly one consumer, and it's hardcoded:

```ts
const gitlab = ProviderV2.ID.make("gitlab")
if (discoveryLoaders[gitlab] && providers[gitlab] && isProviderAllowed(gitlab)) {
  const discovered = await discoveryLoaders[gitlab]()
  // merge, not overwriting existing models
}
```

So the general mechanism shipped and serves a single provider. Separately, providers declared in `opencode.json` only ever get `env`, `name`, and `options` merged, so they can't reach `discoveryLoaders` at all regardless.

Net effect on 1.17.18: a custom `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider still requires every model ID written out by hand, even though its `/v1/models` endpoint answers fine. Working around it today needs a plugin using the `config` hook to fetch `/v1/models` and populate `provider.models` before startup.

#27553 is a duplicate of this issue (filed 2026-05-14).

Would maintainers prefer (a) `models-endpoint` rebased onto `dev`, or (b) a fresh, minimal PR that generalizes the existing call site from the hardcoded `gitlab` lookup to a loop over `discoveryLoaders`, gated on the provider having a `baseURL`? (b) looks like a small diff against current `dev` and avoids resurrecting a 5,700-commit-stale branch. Happy to open it if that's welcome.

This PR (and any associated FR issues) should be re-opened and completed, despite the current automated 'low reaction'-reasoned closure.

The issue with "Close if PR has fewer than 2 positive reactions" is that PRs, like this one, are about fairly obscure stuff that most people won't investigate enough, and therefore will never find a PR like this... but they would've still appreciated it if the PR was completed.

While a popularity contest works well for prioritizing user-facing features, it fails for obscure architectural limitations like tool output truncation because users are unlikely to find and read the `message.state.output` which is inaccessible to the DOM itself, let alone the front-facing UI.

LLMs do not say "I did not read the full thing" or "My response is based on a truncated reading", it will either:
\- respond based on incomplete data - resulting in the user believing the agent gave a 'dumb' or incorrect answer, leading to re-prompting **(and a wastage of tokens)** 
\- it'll attempt to bypass the limit on its own, in many cases, writing python scripts to parse the file, executing them, hitting syntax & run time errors, and recursively solving them **(massively wasting tokens)**.

This isn't just beneficial to users. OpenCode pays for DeepSeek v4 Flash and similar models, if they want to reduce their costs, increasing the truncation limit or providing configurability would do just that. As it reduces the unnecessary wastage of tokens, as discussed earlier, via re-prompting or unnecessary recursive python debugging just to read a file.

I hit this in production-like conditions and got to the exact mechanism.

Root cause: on quota-class 429s, Azure OpenAI returns both retry-after: 30 and retry-after-ms: 0. delay() in packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts gives retry-after-ms priority — and "0" is truthy, parseFloat("0") === 0 passes the NaN guard, so it returns a 0ms delay on every attempt. Combined with the session retry policy having no max attempt count (#21960, #17648), the loop runs at network round-trip speed: I measured ~5 sustained requests/second for ~30 minutes (thousands of requests, zero tokens served, no error surfaced).

Repro: point opencode at a local mock that always answers 429 with both headers above — it hammers at RTT speed. Remove retry-after-ms from the mock and it politely retries every 30s. The diff between those two runs is the bug. (Most mocks only send retry-after, which is why this hides.)

Deterministic check: calling delay(n, error) with responseHeaders: { "retry-after": "30", "retry-after-ms": "0" } returns 0 for any n.

Proposed fix (happy to PR): treat non-positive hints as "no usable hint" — add && parsedMs > 0 / && parsedSeconds > 0 so a zero/negative value falls through (ms → seconds → exponential backoff). With Azure's real headers the delay becomes 30s. A separate PR could add a max attempt count to SessionRetry.policy per #21960. Note: one existing test ("policy updates retry status and increments attempts") uses retry-after-ms: "0" as a fixture and implicitly depends on the 0ms behaviour — it would need a small fixture bump.

> This is intentional, we aren't allowed to include it

Thanks for the duplicate check. I reviewed #27837, #10519, and #28340. My issue shares the same **root cause** as #27837 (SSE race condition: `server.connected` fires before `M.children` is populated), but I believe it's a distinct angle worth tracking separately because:

1. **Context**: #27837 reproduces in a full browser window. My issue only reproduces when the web UI is embedded in a VS Code webview iframe (via the [opencode-chat](https://github.com/kwickramasekara/opencode-chat) extension). In a full browser on the same VPS, sessions load correctly.

2. **Trigger**: The iframe embedding changes the timing characteristics enough to make the race condition **always reproducible**, whereas #27837 in a full browser seems intermittent for some users.

3. **Workaround**: Manually clicking the server icon, then clicking the project from "Recent projects" forces a re-bootstrap and sessions appear. This workaround isn't documented in #27837.

4. **Environment**: Debian VPS via VS Code Remote SSH (not Windows/WSL like #27837), ruling out Windows path resolution as a factor.

If the maintainers prefer to track this under #27837, I'm happy to close this as a duplicate. But I wanted to document the iframe-specific angle since it's a growing use case (VS Code extensions, desktop apps embedding the web UI, etc.) and the reproduction is 100% reliable in this context.

I would love to see this feature too! It is very useful for:

- **Shepherding PRs** (self explanatory)

- [**Gangprompting in Discord**](https://x.com/thdxr/status/2073045223752745189) - Different folks are doing gangprompting with Discord differently:

   - [OpenCode team built their own Discord bot based on OpenCode 2.0](https://x.com/thdxr/status/2064851481669370311), but it's not out yet (been waiting for a month)
   - [Kimaki](https://github.com/remorses/kimaki) is a Discord bot that wraps the OpenCode server, injects its own plugins for deep integration.
   - [Discord OpenCode Bridge](https://github.com/dtinth/discord-opencode-bridge) (I built it) is a standalone Discord bot that connects to an existing OpenCode server without requiring custom plugins.

  However, vanilla Claude Code already supports gangprompting through the [Monitor](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#monitor-tool) tool (the subject of this issue). Here's all I need to do:

  1. Set `DISCORD_TOKEN` in my env.
  2. Give Claude Code the channel ID to loop itself into.

  Claude Code then:

  1. Writes a script that polls Discord for new messages [via the REST API](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/message#get-channel-messages) (it just dumps the message as JSON object, an LLM knows how to parse it)
  2. Runs the script using the Monitor tool → New messages in Discord becomes a synthetic prompt
  3. Curls the [Discord's REST API to respond](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/message#create-message)

  Now the whole team has a direct line to the Claude Code instance. No need to use any fancy plugin.

That's why I think the Monitor tool is one missing primitive that would unlock a lot of possibilities without requiring plugins.
